V. ADVERSE EFFECTS WHICH CANNOT BE AVOIDED SHOULD THE PROPOSAL BE IMPLEMENTED
1. Adverse impacts on individuals who violate provisions of Act and are subject to arrest and fines or confinement could occur. Included among such individuals are all those subject to U.S. jurisdiction; those who attempt to transship endangered animals through the U.S.; those involved in illegal taking a species classed as "likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction;" U.S. subjects who take endangered animals on the high seas; and those who attempt to export endangered animals from the U.S.
2. Adverse impacts on land developers because the Act makes endangered species a competitor for acquisition and control of certain pieces of habitat frequently in high value areas. The ceiling on use of Land and Water Conservation Funds for this purpose would be lifted by the proposed legislation making more species eligible for benefits through land acquisition and increasing lands affected.
3. Adverse poitical impacts on governments due to preempting their authorities to allow the taking of endangered resident species. Under the proposed legislation, authority for regulation or protection of endangered species would rest with the Federal Government until States develop acceptable programs for protection and management of each endangered species.
4. Adverse impacts on individuals due to loss of additional economic and cultural benefits because of greater restriction on the taking of endangered species in the United States. These would be short term impacts since the species involved could not be expected to remain in continuous supply unless restored, in which case they would no longer be endangered.
